title: The PM’s small measures aim to help the public take back control – and we know how powerful that can be | Gaby Hinsliff
summary: E-bikes, noisy headphones, flytipping: Burnham is weighing in on areas that make a difference to how people feel about life, says Guardian columnist Gaby Hinsliff

Imagine waking up one morning to find a humiliating video of you, filmed without your knowledge or control, plastered all over social media. Maybe you were sweating at the gym; or maybe at work, in a bar, or walking down the street, where you never realised the stranger hassling you for your number was covertly filming for his social media channel dedicated to shaming women who won’t date him.
summary_zh: 電動自行車、吵鬧的耳機、非法傾倒垃圾：《衛報》專欄作家加比·欣斯利夫 (Gaby Hinsliff) 表示，伯納姆正在權衡那些能夠改變人們對生活的感受的領域
想像一下，有一天早上醒來，發現一段關於你的羞辱性視頻，該視頻是在你不知情或無法控制的情況下拍攝的，並貼在社交媒體上。也許你在健身房揮汗如雨；或者也許是在工作中、在酒吧里，或者走在街上，你從來沒有意識到那個向你索要電話號碼的陌生人正在秘密拍攝他的社交媒體頻道，該頻道致力於羞辱那些不會與他約會的女性。
